site.title: MyFreeStyle Email Design System
site.intro: 30 modules across 6 categories, distilled from the Voucher Optimization (1–19) and Nudge (1–7) emails. Every module is a locked layout: swap the image and edit the text — nothing else. Each one ships as live, table-based HTML that renders at Desktop 600px and Mobile 375px, in Light and Dark mode.

guidelines.title: Locked layouts
guidelines.body: Modules are fixed compositions. Swap images and edit copy only; don’t re-order rows, change colours or add elements. If a layout doesn’t fit, pick a different module.

guidelines.title: Email order
guidelines.body: Header → one Hero → up to four or five Body modules → Customer Support → optional Poll → Disclaimer. Support and Disclaimer are mandatory in every email.

guidelines.title: Retina images
guidelines.body: Export every image at 2× its displayed size. Specs list the 1× slot size; the HTML displays at 1× with explicit width and height.

guidelines.title: Character counts
guidelines.body: Limits are approximations based on the placeholder copy and the text box width. Real words vary — always check the Mobile preview for wrapping.

guidelines.title: Fonts
guidelines.body: Emails use Calibri, with Arial as the fallback for Gmail and other clients without Calibri. Don’t use web fonts in email.

guidelines.title: Merge fields & MLR
guidelines.body: [Magenta bracketed] text marks dynamic merge fields or MLR-flagged copy. Magenta is an annotation colour only — it must never ship.

guidelines.title: Accessibility
guidelines.body: Keep text at WCAG AA contrast against its background (badges on each colour show the ratio). Every meaningful image needs alt text; never put essential copy in an image.

guidelines.title: Dark mode
guidelines.body: Modules carry light-mode colours inline and switch to the Dark token values through the classes in the email head CSS. Without that CSS, emails fall back to light mode safely.

colours.primaryNote: The yellow + charcoal pairing carries every email. Yellow is the hero surface; charcoal is all type and primary buttons.
colours.secondaryNote: Supporting surfaces, borders and links. Magenta is an MLR / merge-field annotation colour — never ship it as a design colour.

typography.fallbackNote: Gmail and most Android clients don’t have Calibri and render Arial, which runs about 10% wider. Leave headroom in character counts.

scale.sample: See your glucose levels in real time.
*Data on file. Abbott Diabetes Care, Inc.

layout.title: Image swap
layout.value: Replace the image file; keep the slot size

layout.title: Breakpoint
layout.value: Mobile styles apply at ≤ 640 px (ADC template)

layout.title: Rounded corners
layout.value: Outlook (Windows) renders square corners — by design

buttons.note: Pill buttons, label in Calibri Bold 18. Primary flips to white in Dark Mode; yellow stays yellow. Buttons are bulletproof: a rounded table cell for most clients and a VML roundrect for Outlook.

icons.note: Abbott icon set. Icons sit centred in a 64 px circle (Yellow, White, Charcoal or Blue background). Use only these — never draw new icons.

logos.note: MyFreeStyle for relationship emails; product lockups for offer emails. Never recolour, stretch or place the logo on a busy photo.

categories.name: Header
categories.blurb: Fixed. Pick one per email based on journey type.

categories.name: Hero
categories.blurb: Exactly one per email, directly under the header.

categories.name: Body
categories.blurb: Stack freely between the hero and support. Keep to four or five body modules per email.

categories.name: Customer Support
categories.blurb: Mandatory. One per email, always the last content module before the disclaimer.

categories.name: Polls
categories.blurb: Optional zero-party data capture. One per email, and only when each answer maps to a follow-up.

categories.name: Disclaimer
categories.blurb: Mandatory legal footer. Copy is controlled by Regulatory; layout never changes. Always last.

modules.title: Quick pulse · 2 options
modules.description: Short Nudge / conversational emails. Two options only, each a tracked link.
modules.usage: Lightweight yes / no pulse. Derived from POL-01 for short emails where 4 options is too heavy. Locked layout — edit only image fills and text.
notes: Options are outline pills. The 2px ring uses the text/charcoal variable, which turns white in dark mode, and no border-colour utility class exists. The ring is therefore an outer td with padding:2px and mfs-dm-bg-charcoal, around an inner td with mfs-dm-bg-white. Outlook gets a VML roundrect with a 2px stroke instead (no dark flip).

Mobile compromise: the options stack (centred, 8px apart) instead of sitting side by side as in Mobile · Light. In Figma the pair only fits by bleeding into the 32px side padding, and it would overflow at 375px with the Arial fallback (iOS has no Calibri).
VML widths are 216px and 132px. Re-check them if the labels change.
The heading uses mfs-h2 (28→24 on mobile) per CONVENTIONS.

modules.title: Full disclaimer · footnotes + legal + ADC code

notes: Editable: text only — supplied by Regulatory. Never restyle.
Legal type is 13/18 throughout. Figma uses a 1.4/1.3 line height, normalised to the 18px legal token.
Keep the footnote symbols (*) and the [ADC code] / [MM/YY] / [Offer terms…] / [ISI…] placeholders verbatim. The magenta #FF00F5 placeholders must be replaced before send.
Blank lines between footnotes are 18px top padding (one legal line). Block gaps are 24 → 16 on mobile (mfs-pt3).
Footer links are hard-coded #001489 in Figma, even in the Dark frame. They get mfs-dm-link per the CONVENTIONS link rule so they stay readable on #222731.
